title: Injured constable testifies at fatality inquiry
article: An Edmonton police constable who was shot in the moments before a man was fatally wounded by police in 2006 testified Monday at a fatality inquiry into the death of Darren James Cardinal.
Cardinal, 27, died in a shootout with police in a duplex in northeast Edmonton in June 2006.
Const. Dan Furman was one of three officers who responded to a call about a man with a gun at the house.
When Furman arrived, he pulled out his Taser stun gun and led another officer downstairs in search of the man, he testified. The officers found Cardinal hiding in the furnace room.
Furman fired his Taser after Cardinal pointed a pistol at him. But as soon as he did, he heard a loud bang.
The first shot hit Furman's body armour and broke his sternum. Then Cardinal was on top of him and shot him three more times, Furman told the inquiry.
Cardinal fired three more shots that night.
The other officers fired 14, hitting Cardinal up to 10 times. Cardinal died in hospital shortly afterwards when emergency surgery failed to save his life.
Furman suffered a severed major artery, a pierced lung and broken ribs. He lay in a pool of his own blood, thinking he was going to die.
First aid administered by another officer saved his life, Furman said. He ended up spending nearly a week in intensive care.
Cardinal died from the cumulative effects of the gunshot wounds, Alberta's chief medical officer Dr. Graeme Dowling told the inquiry.
"Mr. Cardinal died as a result of several gunshot wounds primarily located over what we would call his trunk or chest and abdomen area," he told reporters outside the inquiry.
"Internally these injuries produced damage to the right lung and the liver that just really couldn't be overcome in spite of the best efforts by some very, very good and qualified surgeons."
After his testimony, Furman said he was relieved it was over.
"It was tough to relive that incident," he said.
Furman told reporters he had no regrets about his actions that night.
The inquiry also heard testimony from one of Cardinal's friends, who said Cardinal had a crack habit.
Police said they found six grams of crack on Cardinal the night he was shot.
Two more officers who were in the house on the night in question are expected to testify on Tuesday.
